These slides were built with coding agents, working from a brief and a run
of corrections.
This page is what I asked for and what I said back, with the typos
corrected.
The [AIandIDVUB prompts page](https://samabbott.co.uk/AIandIDVUB/prompts.html)
does the same for an earlier talk.

## How these slides were built

{{< video figures/agents-deck.mp4 title="The finished slides, with the build played back beside them" >}}

The video plays the finished slides beside a replay of the build, with some of my steers as I sent them.

One Claude Code session, running Claude Opus, built the deck on 2 November 2026 between about 12:50 and 19:30 UTC.
I sent it 183 messages, most of them short steers sent while it was still working on the last one.
It replied in about 520 model turns and made 587 tool calls.
Most were shell commands (392), to render the deck, take screenshots, query GitHub and commit.
The rest were file reads (161), web fetches (13), messages to a subagent (7), file writes (4), subagent launches (4), skills (2), tool searches (2) and questions back to me (2).

Four subagents did side jobs, with 210 tool calls between them.

| Subagent | Tool calls |
|---|---|
| Find figures from other groups, including 19 web searches | 72 |
| Review the first draft | 32 |
| Review the second draft | 37 |
| Draw the agent, multi-agent and time schematics | 69 |

The repository has about 90 commits from the session, all by seabbs-bot with me as co-author.

The session ran from about 12:50 to 19:30 UTC, but I was not prompting for all of it.
I went for a swim, walked the dog, had a meeting and ran agents on other projects, so I think I gave it about two hours of attention.
At API prices for Claude Opus 5.5 the tokens would cost about $60, most of it re-reading the cached context on each turn.
These counts come from the session logs and are a snapshot from late in the build.
